transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-21
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Samira Khan (Redwood AE), Ethan Brooks (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (AuroraPay - Head of ML), Marc Chen (AuroraPay - SRE), Priya Iyer (AuroraPay - VP Product)

Summary:
Redwood Optimize walkthrough focused on batching and prefix/KV cache recommendations for AuroraPay's conversational payments assistant. Discussed latency vs cost tradeoffs, expected cost savings from KV/prefix caching for long-context RAG, and next steps to run a 2-week pilot with benchmark scripts. Security and VPC questions surfaced (KMS/SOC2/SAML).

Topics covered:
- Current infra & traffic profile
- Batching strategies and continuous batching implications
- Prefix (request-level) caching vs kv cache for retrieved context
- Cost model examples and estimated savings for AuroraPay volume
- Pilot plan and security checklist

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samira: hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick intros — i'm samira from redwood, ae on the account, and ethan's our se who will run the deep stuff. you good to go lena?
[00:12] Lena: yep thanks, lena here, head of ml, excited to see the optimize walkthrough, we run a convo assistant that fetches payment history and policy docs — long context, lots of retrieval.
[00:22] Ethan: cool, quick agenda: we'll look at batching, then prefix cache and kv cache tradeoffs, show a cost model, then action items. feel free to interrupt.
[00:30] Marc: small ask — our SRE needs latency numbers for SLOs, and we need to know networking for private deployments.
[00:36] Samira: noted, we'll include per-route p50/p95 numbers and a checklist for vpc/kms.

[02:05] Ethan: starting with batching — two quick points: continuous batching increases throughput by grouping inflight requests into a single GPU batch. for small requests we see 2-3x throughput improvements, for larger token lengths the benefit reduces. for aurorapay, based on your median request of ~120 tokens and peak QPS ~60, we estimate batching can improve effective throughput ~2.5x.
[02:42] Lena: when you say 2.5x that's for hosted or dedicated?
[02:47] Ethan: good question — that estimate assumes dedicated or reserved capacity where you can tune batch windows. hosted can still get batching but more conservative; think 1.6-2x in hosted at our observed loads.

[05:10] Ethan: next — prefix cache (we sometimes call request-level cache) vs kv cache. prefix cache stores common prompt prefixes (like system + static instructions) and cached model KV states for repeated starts; it's great when many requests share the same opening context. kv cache is for retrieved content: you fetch docs into a key-value store (compressed kv pages) so the model doesn't re-tokenize or re-run expensive attention over large retrieved text.
[05:45] Priya: so prefix cache helps with repeated system prompts, kv cache helps with retrieval-augmented generation where the model must access long policy docs?
[05:51] Ethan: exactly. for your use-case, both help: prefix cache speeds up the common template around payments verification and disclaimers; kv cache reduces per-token compute for long retrieved chunks — combined they compound savings.

[08:00] Ethan: hit rates are the important metric. example: if prefix cache hit is 60% and kv cache hit is 55% on the retrieved chunks, you can expect token generation compute to drop by roughly 40% given overlap, though exact numbers depend on sequence lengths and overlap.
[08:25] Lena: can you show a worked cost model?
[08:30] Ethan: sure — high level: baseline (no cache, no batching) at your traffic = 1M generated tokens/day -> ~30M tokens/month. using our conservative hosted pricing, that's around $X (we'll send tailored numbers) but in sample math: baseline cost = $12k/month. with batching (2.5x throughput on dedicated) your effective cost per unit falls because you need fewer GPUs or lower reservation; combine batching + 40% token reduction from caches -> net savings ~50-60%. so example: $12k -> $5.5k/month. numbers are illustrative — we'll run your exact workload in the pilot.
[09:12] Marc: those look substantial, can you explain where the savings come from again?
[09:18] Ethan: batching reduces idle token compute by improving utilization. kv/prefix caching reduces tokens that the model actually computes over, and avoids repeated attention on static text. quantization and model choice also play in — e.g., using a 4-bit quantized variant reduces cost further at small accuracy tradeoffs.

[11:40] Lena: are there accuracy regressions when using kv cache? we've seen hallucinations when slicing documents incorrectly.
[11:47] Ethan: good callout — kv cache itself doesn't change model output semantics if done correctly — it's essentially caching intermediate KV states for exact suffixes; the risk is stale retrievals or incorrect chunking. we recommend validation evals on a holdout prompt set. we have automatic regression alerts in Redwood Optimize tied to prompt sets.

[14:05] Samira: security — AuroraPay asked about KMS and audit logs?
[14:12] Marc: yeah, and SOC 2 scope, plus can we run in our VPC or on-prem?
[14:18] Ethan: short answer: yes. Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem bundles; we integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key management, we emit audit logs for per-request traces, and our hosted offering is SOC 2 certified. we'll send the security pack with integrations.
[14:40] Marc: great, and what about SSO?
[14:43] Samira: SAML/SSO + RBAC available for enterprise plans, we'll include our SSO doc.

[18:05] Ethan: back to performance — here's a realistic microbenchmark: on A100-ish hardware, 1 GPU running our inference runtime handles X tokens/s baseline; with batching (batch window 30-50ms) you get ~2.2x throughput; with prefix/KV cache hits at 60% you drop compute for those requests to near zero for the cached portion, so end-to-end latency for hits is dominated by network and small model remainder. p50 drops by ~40-60ms for hits in our measurements.
[19:00] Lena: do you have sample configs for batch window and max_batch_size?
[19:05] Ethan: yes, sample configs: batch_window_ms=50, max_batch_size=64 for your median; but we'll tune in pilot. we'll attach the sample config + perf dashboard.

[22:30] Priya: what's the operational complexity to run kv cache? does it require extra infra from our side?
[22:36] Ethan: two options: managed kv (we handle storage & eviction) or customer-managed (you provide S3-like store + index). managed is simplest; customer-managed gives you full control and data residency. both integrate with the runtime; eviction is LRU/time-based. for heavy retrievals we recommend wrap-around sharding.

[26:00] Lena: any guardrails for regression detection? we can't afford production drops.
[26:06] Ethan: yes, Redwood Optimize supports evals and regression alerts tied to prompt suites. we can set thresholds on quality metrics and auto-fallback to full model (no cache) or different model variants if QoR drops.

[30:20] Samira: pricing and pilot — recommended pilot: 2 weeks, dedicated reserved pool for a small commit, we'll run your traffic sample, run benchmarks, and produce a cost model. deliverables: perf dashboard, per-route cost breakdown, and a checklist for production rollout.
[30:40] Marc: for the pilot we'll need a network diagram and an ops contact. i'll be the ops contact.
[30:46] Marc: also, do you have a template SOW?
[30:49] Samira: yes, we'll send a template pilot SOW and pricing.

[34:55] Ethan: quick example numbers pulled from a prior customer (anonymized): baseline monthly token cost $18k, after batching & kv cache savings 62% -> $6.8k. in that engagement prefix hits were 58% and kv hits 47%. your expected hit rates are similar given shared templates and retrieval patterns.
[36:10] Lena: what are typical tradeoffs for accuracy if we quantize?
[36:16] Ethan: 4-bit quant can have negligible impact on many tasks but depends on your evals; we recommend running quantized evals as part of pilot. if degradation seen, fallback rules can route sensitive routes to higher-precision variants.

[40:00] Priya: any competitors we should be aware of on this? we looked at vertex and openai earlier.
[40:07] Samira: vertex offers managed endpoints but less opinionated optimize tooling; openai has a good hosted API but you lose private deployment flexibility and cost controls; Mistral and some infra vendors have fast runtimes but fewer integrated rollout/alerting features. we'll include a short comparison doc.

[44:50] Marc: network requirements for private: we'll need peering, specific firewall rules, and a list of FQDNs.
[44:58] Ethan: we'll send the network checklist and a minimal test harness for connectivity.

[47:20] Samira: recap / next steps: 1) Samira sends pricing + SOW + security pack; 2) Ethan shares benchmark scripts, sample configs, and perf dashboard link; 3) Marc confirms ops/VPC peering details; 4) schedule pilot kickoff for the week of 2026-05-25. anyone disagree?
[47:45] Priya: sounds good.
[47:48] Lena: good plan.
[47:50] Marc: i'll get the network details by monday.

[50:00] Samira: thanks all, we'll follow up with materials and calendar invite for pilot kickoff.
[50:06] (crosstalk) Ethan: thanks. bye.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional mis-heard acronyms (KV pronounced as K V cash), filler words and small disfluencies present.
